checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A full-length Picatinny rail runs along the top of the upper receiver and handguard, equipped with flip-up iron sights.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The Picatinny rail slots appear slightly 'mushy' or fused together rather than having sharp, distinct mechanical edges. The texture lacks the crisp machining marks expected on metal.
The fingers wrapping around the vertical foregrip/handguard blend slightly into the weapon structure. The thumb position is ambiguous and seems to merge with the rail.
The night-vision goggle mount on the helmet appears slightly asymmetrical and floats somewhat unnaturally above the brim, lacking a clear connection point.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific model variant (e.g., M4/M16/AR-15 platform) and ensure it matches the 'assault rifle' class label accurately.
To rigorously check for fusion artifacts between the user's fingers and the weapon's handgrip/foregrip, a common AI failure mode.
To verify that the flip-up sights and rail segments have correct depth separation and are not bleeding into the background or each other.
To assess general coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global distortions or 'AI sheen'.

focus_areas: Mechanical precision of the Picatinny rail slots (sharpness vs melting)
Anatomical correctness of fingers gripping the weapon (no fusion/extra digits)
Structural integrity of the helmet-mounted accessories
Consistency of the magazine insertion point
